title: Third-Party Audit Storyboard & SIEM Evidence Playbook (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical storyboard and playbook for preparing SIEM exports, RBAC v2 evidence, and narrative artifacts that we give to customers during third-party security assessments (SOC2 readiness, customer questionnaire deep-dives, or bespoke audit requests). It is intentionally pragmatic — a sequence of "scenes" auditors expect, the evidence files we attach, and the short explanatory text to accompany each artifact so auditors don’t have to guess context.

Audience:
- Customer security teams and external auditors requesting technical evidence
- Internal Responder: Security & Compliance engineers and Solutions Engineers supporting a live audit

High-level goals:
1) Create an audit narrative that maps directly to artifacts (no mystery, minimal back-and-forth).
2) Provide SIEM export snippets and RBAC v2 traces that are script-friendly and ready for ingestion.
3) Prioritize evidence that is reproducible and defensible (timestamped, minimally redacted, accompanied by an extraction note).

Quick runbook (one-paragraph checklist):
- Kickoff: Confirm scope + controls in-scope (e.g., logging, access control, encryption). Save a scope file.
- Storyboard: Pick 3 representative auditor queries (login, admin-change, data-export) and map them to log folders and RBAC snapshots.
- Export: Generate SIEM CSV/NDJSON from time windows tied to those queries, include query used, and a checksum.
- Annotate: For each artifact add a 2–3 sentence "extraction note" that explains provenance and any redactions.
- Deliver: Package with index.json and a short narrative PDF.

Storyboard: scenes and artifacts
Scene 1: Admin role modification (RBAC v2)- Scenario: Auditor wants to verify the request/approval flow for privilege elevation and the resulting audit log entries.- Artifacts to provide: RBAC v2 role definition export (roles.json), admin-change audit log slice (NDJSON), approval ticket link (Jira key or internal change ticket), ephemeral access token lifecyle note.- Extraction note (example): "roles.json exported from config-db at 2026-02-20T16:03Z. admin-change-logs.ndjson produced by SIEM export query 'event_type:role_update AND actor_type:user' for 2026-02-19T00:00Z..2026-02-21T00:00Z. UUIDs partially redacted; full ids available under NDA."

Scene 2: Service-to-service credential rotation and KMS usage- Scenario: Auditor wants proof that key rotation and KMS usage produce actionable audit events and that usage is restricted by service roles.- Artifacts: KMS operation logs (CSV), SIEM 'kms-access' event slice, sample service principal policy, rotation runbook snapshot.- Extraction note: "KMS logs exported from cloud-kms for project redwood-prod. SIEM normalization preserved 'principal' and 'operation' fields. Rotation runbook v1.2 attached for process context."

Scene 3: User session / data access trace (customer data access)- Scenario: Show that data access is tied to identity and that any abnormal access triggers detection.- Artifacts: Auth token issuance log, session start/stop events, data-read audit events filtered for customer X dataset, alert runbook (if an alert fired).- Extraction note: "Session traces tied to bearer token hash HXXXX (redacted) for user bsmith@customer.com between 2025-12-14T09:00Z and 2025-12-14T09:12Z. SIEM query attached. Alerts correlated with read-volume anomaly."

Evidence file naming conventions- Use short, predictable names: <control>-<artifact>-<YYYYMMDD>-<window>-<format> e.g., rbac-role-change-20260219-20260221-ndjson.ndjson- Include a companion <artifact>-meta.txt for each file that documents: how exported, who ran it, query string, checksum, and redactions performed.

SIEM export patterns and sample queries
- Provide 3 canonical export queries (elastic/splunk/sql-like) we use internally and provide as-is to customers. Include example output columns expected.
- Example (elastic-like):
  index:redwood-logs-* | query: event.type: "role_update" AND outcome: "success" | fields: [@timestamp, actor.id, actor.email, role.name, change.diff, request.id]
- Example (splunk-like):
  search index=prod_logs event=login | stats count by user, src_ip | where count > 5
- Output format recommendations: NDJSON for event slices (one JSON object per line), compressed CSV for metrics summaries, and SHA256 checksums for each compressed artifact.

RBAC v2 evidence checklist (compact)
- Static: role definitions and effective permission matrix (time-versioned snapshot).
- Dynamic: role assignment/change events with actor identity and request id.
- Validation: policy evaluation logs (if available) or sample policy evaluation trace for 2–3 requests.
- Access review artifacts: periodic attestation reports, reviewer identities, and timestamps.

Packaging and delivery
- Index file (index.json) containing: list of artifacts, short description lines, extraction note for each, and MD5/SHA256 checksums. Provide both machine-readable index.json and a human-friendly index.pdf that narrates the flow.
- Delivery channels: secure link to signed S3 bucket with short TTL, or direct transfer to auditor SFTP. Include a manifest and PGP-signed index if requested by customer.

Handling sensitive identifiers and redaction policy- Default policy: redact PII and customer-specific identifiers in delivered artifacts unless explicit customer consent. Replace with deterministic hashed tokens and include mapping under NDA if required.
- Redaction note format (example): "replaced email domains with @redacted.example; preserved local-part hashed with SHA256(seed=2026-02-20)."

Common auditor questions and scripted answers
- Q: "How do you prove the log stream hasn’t been tampered with?"
  A: "We provide SIEM export with exporter process audit trail and S3 object checksums, plus cloud provider immutable storage metadata where applicable."
- Q: "Can we see full identifiers?"
  A: "We can provide full identifiers under a mutual NDA; otherwise we provide deterministic hashes and a mapping process explanation."

Operational templates (copy/paste friendly)
- Extraction note template:
  "Artifact: <filename>
   Exported by: <name/email>
   Exported at: <UTC timestamp>
   Query: <query text>
   Time window: <start..end>
   Redaction: <what was redacted>
   Provenance: <S3 path or db-snapshot-id>
   Checksum: <sha256>
"
- SIEM query template (elastic-like):
  "POST /_search
   {
     \"query\": {
       \"bool\": {
         \"must\": [ { \"term\": { \"event.type\": \"role_update\" } }, { \"term\": { \"outcome\": \"success\" } } ],
         \"filter\": { \"range\": { \"@timestamp\": { \"gte\": \"2026-02-19T00:00:00Z\", \"lte\": \"2026-02-21T00:00:00Z\" } } }
       }
     },
     \"_source\": [\"@timestamp\", \"actor.id\", \"actor.email\", \"role.name\", \"change.diff\", \"request.id\"]
   }
"

Customer-facing narrative (1-page template)
- Opening: short summary of scope, dates, and controls demonstrated.
- What we delivered: table of artifacts (name, short description, extraction note).
- How to verify: commands to compute checksums and sample queries to reproduce slices.
- Redactions & limitations: transparent list of what is redacted and how to obtain full data if needed (NDA path).

Escalation play (if auditor requests more):
- Triage: Solutions Engineer collects additional context and assigns SEC-OPS owner.
- Timeline: 48-hour response SLA for targeted followups; 5 business days for additional full exports requiring deep hold or legal review.
- When to involve legal: requests for unredacted PII or wholesale log exports flagged by SEC-OPS.

Appendix A: Minimal SIEM export field map (recommended)- timestamp: iso8601- event.id: uuid- event.type: string- actor.id: uuid or hashed id- actor.type: user/service- actor.email: optional hashed- resource.id: uuid or hashed- resource.type: dataset/table/endpoint- change.diff: text (if applicable)- request.id: uuid

Appendix B: Example artifact index (human readable)
- rbac-role-change-20260219-20260221-ndjson.ndjson (3.2MB) — admin role updates and actor details (redacted emails). See rbac-role-change-20260219-20260221-meta.txt- kms-ops-20260201-20260228.csv.gz (120KB) — KMS operations for rotation events. See kms-ops-20260201-20260228-meta.txt- session-trace-custX-20251214-ndjson.ndjson (4.8MB) — data access for customer X, token hashed. See session-trace-custX-meta.txt

Open questions / items for follow-up- Automate generation of index.json and checksums via a single CLI tool (SEC-EXPORT) — owner: Julian Park (SEC-OPS).
- Determine canonical time-window length for typical auditor requests (30 days default?) — action: SEC lead to propose.
- Add pre-approved NDA attachment template for expedited full-identifier releases.

Document history and notes- v0.1 2025-11-02: Initial brainstorming and checklist (A. Chen).
- v0.2 2026-01-12: Added SIEM query templates and RBAC v2 checklist (D. Martinez).
- v0.3 2026-02-28: Added packaging guidance and escalation SLA (P. Nair).

End of document.
